summary: Sprint 14 P1 Bloc 4 (bookings + missions + interventions migration) verified. Full pytest suite ran THREE times consecutively against http://localhost:8001. Run 1: 485/485 passed. Runs 2 & 3: 484/485 passed with the SAME flake: tests/test_phase3_ai_missions.py::test_missions_mine_lists_own — caused by data pollution on client.test@proconnect.fr (515 missions in DB) combined with routes/missions.py:238-244 using unordered `db.missions.find(...).to_list(500)` then sorting in Python AFTER the fetch, so newly-created missions may fall outside the 500-doc window. This is a Bloc-4 regression (pagination/ordering must happen in Mongo). All 22 dedicated Bloc-4 tests (tests/test_sprint14_p1_bloc4_mission_flow.py) pass. All 5 requested security guarantees verified via direct HTTP: (1) unauth pro_accept=>401, client pro_accept=>403 'Réservé aux artisans'; (2) stranger GET/cancel/accept intervention => 404 (never 403); (3) illegal booking pending→completed=>400, cancelled→accepted=>400, double-cancel intervention=>400; (4) atomic double-accept: first artisan wins with 200, second gets 409; (5) simulated flags: intervention has simulated+price_simulated, mission has simulated+price_estimated, booking has simulated.

regression_vs_baseline_383: No regression on the 383 baseline. Bloc-4 added 22 new tests. Total collected = 485. The 1 flaky failure (test_missions_mine_lists_own) is data-dependent and pre-existing at the state-machine level, exposed by the Bloc-4 migration of routes/missions.py which drops in-DB ordering — see RCA below.

minor.issue: Bloc-4 migration regression. routes/missions.py:238-244 fetches `db.missions.find(...).to_list(500)` WITHOUT a Mongo-side sort, then sorts by created_at in Python. On accounts with >500 lifetime missions (e.g., client.test@proconnect.fr has 515), the newest missions may be excluded from the unordered 500-doc window, so /missions/mine misses them → test_missions_mine_lists_own flakes. Fix: use `db.missions.find({...}).sort('created_at', -1).limit(500)` in Mongo. Same pattern should be audited on interventions/bookings mine endpoints.

action_items: Fix routes/missions.py:238-244 — add Mongo-side sort+limit on /missions/mine: `db.missions.find({'client_id': user['user_id']}, {'_id': 0}).sort('created_at', -1).to_list(500)`. This will make test_phase3_ai_missions.py::test_missions_mine_lists_own deterministic on polluted test accounts.
Audit routes/interventions.py and routes/bookings.py `/mine` endpoints for the same unordered-fetch-then-Python-sort anti-pattern.
Optionally add a `TEST_` prefix cleanup fixture for phase3 tests to purge accumulated fixture data (515 missions on client.test@proconnect.fr).
critical_code_review_comments: routes/missions.py `/missions/mine`: sort must live in the DB query, not in Python, when combined with `to_list(N)` — otherwise pagination is non-deterministic on datasets larger than N.
seed_data_creation: Spot-check script /tmp/bloc4_spot_check.py registers 2 ephemeral artisans + 1 ephemeral other-client per run and creates 3 missions / 2 bookings / 2 interventions under client.test@auxora.fr. No persistent seed changes. All test data uses random UUID emails.

Only lingering issue is the flake on tests/test_phase3_ai_missions.py::test_missions_mine_lists_own caused by unordered `to_list(500)` in routes/missions.py:240 combined with 515+ accumulated missions on client.test@proconnect.fr. Fix is a one-liner Mongo sort. After fix, re-run 3x to confirm 485/485 x 3.
rca_of_issue: REPRO: `pytest tests/test_phase3_ai_missions.py::test_missions_mine_lists_own -v` (fails ~2/3 of the time). ROOT CAUSE: /app/backend/routes/missions.py lines 238-244 execute `ms = await db.missions.find({'client_id': user['user_id']}, {'_id': 0}).to_list(500)` then `ms.sort(key=lambda x: x.get('created_at', ''), reverse=True)`. Because MongoDB returns documents in undefined order without an explicit .sort(), and the client account client.test@proconnect.fr has 515 lifetime missions in the DB (verified via count_documents), the freshly-created fixture mission is often outside the truncated 500-doc slice. MITIGATION: change to `.sort('created_at', -1).to_list(500)` so the newest 500 are always returned. Alternatively, cap fixture data via TEST_ prefix cleanup fixture.
